title: ChristianaCare Epic go-live, official July 2026 update
dek: Oct. 3, 2026 date and training gate from the newsroom.
body: ChristianaCare’s July 2026 newsroom update scheduled an Oct. 3, 2026 Epic go-live and said the system was in the final stage, with less than three months remaining. COO Ric Cuming said training mixes on-demand modules with live, role-based instruction, and that readiness checks are meant to make sure caregivers finish required training before they use the new system. The same update said that once ChristianaCare is live, all Delaware health systems — and many in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Maryland — will be on Epic, with Care Everywhere for outside visits. Patients are told to keep appointments unless ChristianaCare contacts them.
impactSentence: Oct. 3 is a training-gated cutover on ChristianaCare’s own update.

title: Jefferson FY2026 operating loss, plus Fitch liquidity
dek: Inquirer year-end $181.5 million to bondholders; Fitch $5.5 billion / 119 DCOH through March 31. Not a swap.
body: The Inquirer, Aug. 14, 2026, reported that Thomas Jefferson University and Jefferson Health posted a $181.5 million operating loss for the year ended June 30, 2026, after a $208 million loss the prior year, in results reported to bondholders. As the Inquirer read that packet: $112 million in layoff and related costs after the Aug. 1, 2024 Lehigh Valley Health Network close; $17.7 billion revenue (from $15.8 billion); a $130.3 million Jefferson Health Plans loss on 415,172 members; and a climb from a $103.8 million first-quarter operating loss to a $71.1 million fourth-quarter operating profit. CFO Michael Harrington said commercial-insurer actions in Pennsylvania threaten those gains. Jefferson sued Independence Blue Cross over contract reinterpretations and sued Aetna in April over Medicare Advantage stay payments. Independence said it acts for its customers. Aetna said its policies comply with federal law. This desk has not opened the EMMA year-end PDF. Separately, Fitch on June 18, 2026 assigned F1+ to TJU taxable CP notes, affirmed the A IDR with a Negative Outlook, and cited $5.5 billion unrestricted liquidity and about 119 days cash on hand for fiscal 2026 year-to-date through March 31, 2026, including the health plan and excluding line-of-credit draws and about $1.1 billion donor-restricted funds. Fitch cited about $15.5 billion operating revenue for the year ended June 30, 2025, and about $112 million Jefferson Health Plan losses through the first nine months of both FY2025 and FY2026. Those nine-month figures are not a substitute for the June 30 year-end loss.
impactSentence: The $181.5 million year-end operating loss sits next to $5.5 billion / 119 DCOH through March 31; Harrington says the climb holds only if commercial contracts do.

title: Penn in-house scribe headcount and 2024 JAMA pilot table
dek: Some 1,200 ambulatory users in the Inquirer clip. A separate 46-clinician 2024 QI study used DAX Copilot (Nuance). Not the same product sentence.
body: The Philadelphia Inquirer, Nov. 10, 2025, said Dina Capalongo, a Penn Medicine internist, uses an AI scribe Penn designed in-house: she hits a green button on a phone app, ambient listening drafts a sectioned note she still has to approve, usually before she leaves the room. The same clip said some 1,200 Penn Medicine providers were using an AI scribe in ambulatory and outpatient offices. Mitchell Schnall said the system built its own scribe. A separate JAMA Network Open study (Duggan et al., published Feb. 19, 2025; outpatient QI April–June 2024 at one Philadelphia academic system) gave clinicians a commercially available ambient scribe, DAX Copilot (Nuance). Among 46 clinicians in 17 specialties, the abstract associated that tool with 20.4% less time in notes per appointment (10.3 to 8.2 minutes; P<.001), 9.3% greater same-day appointment closure (66.2% to 72.4%), and 30.0% less after-hours work time (50.6 to 35.4 minutes per workday). Those percents are the abstract cells, not the Table 2 model change-%. Penn Medicine’s Feb. 21, 2025 news release quoted Kevin B. Johnson, who leads the AI4AI Lab, calling those “early but promising results,” and said volunteer clinicians were using the tool with patient permission. That release does not name DAX. The 1,200 in-house count is not the study n and is not DAX. Temple Dragon counts are not this count.
impactSentence: Some 1,200 is an Inquirer headcount for Penn’s later in-house tool; 20.4% less time in notes is a 46-clinician journal table from a 2024 DAX Copilot pilot, not that headcount.

title: Temple Dragon Copilot user count and TUHS cash days
dek: HealthTech 400 end users. Unaudited TUHS 116 DCOH at June 30, 2025.
body: HealthTech Magazine, August 2026, said Benjamin Slovis has a Microsoft Dragon Copilot rollout to 400 end users and quoted him that the tool is “not yet a silver bullet.” HealthTech identified him as chief medical information officer at Philadelphia-based Temple Health. Temple’s June 8, 2026 newsroom note, which names him Chief Medical Information Officer for Temple University Hospital, said he described Dragon Ambient eXperience (DAX) Copilot to the Bucks County Herald: it records the visit and drafts a note the doctor reviews. Separately, Temple University Health System’s unaudited year-end investor report for June 30, 2025 showed 116 days cash on hand (124 at June 30, 2024). That line is not a Copilot, user, or after-hours metric. Penn 1,200 and JAMA 46 are not this count.
impactSentence: Dragon Copilot is at 400 end users in the HealthTech clip; 116 DCOH is an unaudited TUHS year-end line, not a Copilot KPI.
